metadata.description: A ZFS dataset or zvol, a dialect of Volume (CLS-004): the consumer orders a volume and ZFS is how one host-local provider realizes it — a mounted dataset when `volume_mode` is filesystem, a zvol when block. Inherits capacity (the quota or volsize), access mode and volume mode; adds the ZFS-native mountpoint, reported usage and passthrough properties. Carved from a StoragePool, it cannot outlive its pool; datasets nest. Snapshot and replication policy belongs to the control plane, not here.

access_mode.description: Attachment concurrency: `read_write_once`, `read_only_many`, `read_write_many`, `read_write_once_pod` (the Kubernetes PVC access modes, snake_case).

storage_class.description: Reference to the StorageClass that provisions it; authored by handle, resolved later if the class is not yet defined.

reclaim_policy.description: What happens to the data when the consumer releases the volume: Retain or Delete.

disk_entry.description: The `disks[].name` on the Machine this volume realizes; set exactly when the `realizes_disk` edge is declared. Reconvergence joins on it to fill the machine's `realized_volumes`.

data_source.description: What the volume is filled from when it is created: a VolumeSnapshot (a restore) or another Volume (a clone). Absent means it starts empty.

mountpoint.description: Filesystem mountpoint when `volume_mode` is filesystem (/export/gitlab); `none` or `-` if unmounted.

properties.description: Provider passthrough dataset properties (compression, recordsize, mountpoint inheritance).

volume_handle.description: Provider volume handle/id once Realized (CSI volumeHandle / Swordfish Volume Id).

attached.description: Whether the volume is currently attached to a consumer.

accessible_from.description: Where the volume can be attached from, as the provider reports it once Realized (CSI `accessible_topology`, a Kubernetes PV `nodeAffinity`): References to the narrowest scope that reaches it, a Machine.BareMetalHost for host-local storage, a StorageCluster for storage any of its clients can attach, a Location for a site. Placement reads it to put a consumer where its volume is, and a move reads it to tell a re-bind (the target machine is in scope) from a copy (it is not, so a new volume is filled through `data_source`). Each entry a Reference (common-elements §2.5). Absent means the provider did not say, never "anywhere".

relationships.name: provisioned_by
relationships.description: The StorageCluster that provisions this volume (binds its block_storage_class / file_storage_class output). A volume cannot outlive its provisioning cluster.

relationships.name: attaches_to
relationships.description: The consumer(s) this volume is attached to (RWX volumes attach to many). attaches_to is the same relation IPAddress uses for interface attachment — the consumable-resource-to-consumer edge.

relationships.name: realizes_disk
relationships.description: Declared on the volume: this volume realizes one named disk of a Machine, joining on the disk name carried in spec.disk_entry (the edge itself carries no qualifier).

relationships.name: restored_from
relationships.description: The snapshot this volume was filled from (spec.data_source names it). Lineage, read at provisioning.

relationships.name: cloned_from
relationships.description: The volume this one was cloned from (spec.data_source names it). Lineage, read at provisioning.

relationships.name: pool
relationships.description: The pool this dataset is carved from; the dataset cannot outlive its pool.

relationships.name: parent_dataset
relationships.description: The parent dataset in the hierarchy (e.g. aspen/nc/data → aspen/nc), when nested.

relationships.name: host
relationships.description: The host the pool (and thus this dataset) is local to.

adopts.role: consumable-volume request vocabulary (capacity, accessModes, volumeMode, storageClass, reclaimPolicy, dataSource) and the CSI accessible-topology semantics behind `accessible_from`
storage-volume-as-asset vocabulary (CapacityBytes, AccessCapabilities) — same family as StorageCluster

context.purpose: Models a ZFS dataset or zvol carved from a host-local pool — the mounted filesystem or block device host workloads use.
context.plain_description: A volume realized by ZFS on one host: its `volume_mode` says whether it is a mounted dataset (`filesystem`) or a zvol block device (`block`); its `capacity` is the quota or volsize; `mountpoint`, reported passthrough `properties` are the ZFS-native details. It is what a podman container or host service bind-mounts, so it is the storage node those workloads depend on. Volumes nest (parent chains) and cannot outlive the pool they are carved from. Snapshot and replication policy is orchestration, not stored here.
use_when: You need host services and containers tied to the specific dataset they store on, so the dataset outlives them in shutdown order.
You need the pool → dataset → workload chain explicit for capacity and migration planning.
not_for: The pool it is carved from — StoragePool owns the drives and redundancy.
Cluster-provisioned volumes a platform attaches — order at Volume, or a Type of another provisioner; a ZFS volume is host-local.
A network share exported to other machines — FileShare exposes storage; this is the local storage itself.
works_with: StoragePool — the pool the volume is carved from.
Machine.BareMetalHost — the host the volume is local to.
Volume.ZFS — the parent dataset, when nested.
